The Senate Leadership Fund — a powerful GOP super PAC — announced they are shifting resources from another state to launch a massive ad campaign here in Kansas in support of my opponent. This is a major development. If you still had any doubts that this Senate seat is up for grabs, this news should put those to rest. What we do now to respond to this news will determine if we win or lose this race. That’s why my team and I set a $250,000 daily goal to make sure we have the resources to fight back with just 13 days until the election. = If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | = Why is this happening? Because Roger Marshall and his allies are terrified of our grassroots momentum. They’ve seen the polls tightening. They’ve seen the election forecasters upgrading our chance. They’ve seen everyone from Nate Silver to Fox News to The New York Times to The Cook Political Report saying what six months ago seemed impossible: We can really flip this Kansas Senate seat. Now, Marshall’s allies are pouring millions into Kansas to stop it from happening. The scary thing is: If we let them outspend us and drown out our message, their plan might work. What breaks my heart is that Kansas families will suffer. What can we do about it? We fight back. We increase our ad buys, up our canvassing and phone banking efforts, and make sure Kansans far and wide know that there is a different way forward than the chaos and corruption we’re currently seeing from Washington. Peter, it's Michele Tafoya.

I've been on the road a lot recently, pressed for time, hopping from one city to the next, but I still wanted to take some time out of my day to write to you.I didn't waste time sending this to my team for final review; I wanted to get this over to you as soon as I possibly could.

If you've been following what's happening in Minnesota, here's where we're at now:
1. The latest polls now have me and my Far Left opponent, Peggy Flanagan, DEAD EVEN in the home stretch. Voters are clearly demanding change.
2. My campaign has been surging past our expectations thanks to thousands of grassroots patriots like you chipping in just $5 or $10 whenever they can (contrary to my socialist opponent's wealthy boosters).
3. The Democrat political machine has invested thousands in bogus attack ads in Minnesota against me because they're terrified of us pulling off the upset.

It's clear now, more than ever, that the tides are turning in our direction. I wanted to show you, in these points above, some of the fruits of all of our hard work together.
__But the final buzzer still hasn 't sounded, and you don't get a prize for winning the 3rd quarter when there's plenty of time left in the game!__
I've seen first-hand PLENTY of teams who think they've got the win in the bag take their foot off the gas and go on defense... all to face defeat right before the clock hits zero.
**We won 't be that team.**
If anything, we're itching to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat. We've known since the start of this movement that we're the clear underdog in this race.
But we're FAR from throwing in the towel.
Now that we're in the home stretch, your direct support to me and this movement becomes even more important.
Truth be told, it'd be a disaster if we lost you, Peter.
[That’s why I’m asking you today, one final time, to please chip in at least $5 or $10 to help us keep up with Peggy and the Democrats’ wealthy donors.](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=e53e72775b334915bb42dbac492371f2&_e=XuWIS2vv0Yxqw7dmgjdNxGwZwrWaysl4X46PIc4_gZRm30L8bsVT-tF8S08EndAi0K3W2fjoDDjOe85YXnjRS1uUDTMy5GBRTJcoLVS5IxFwrC1EGdnd63-MtDyYHoVhU44lc6gdNb4xpISZsulahA6UKdvCH4UKHnv615Q8Aoo_XEZIq4k8Nmj63yEBk4_pr38wFxCoujqsqIGouB82uQG6Wyib4hgnj8h0lQhxxfIkQKdJo35dRfWmOSOG5pd2E6RiEAjiXwDUC_Mfb2RYYICx8vScjYvQbus4ks4Wi3ilQymZQxNalRdrvnsxd1YdnvmQ1MolTg8oEhULVvWFwfnc7savyfII_GbanYKlkTQ1LoxVYisqhepU-tr1x9WteBGaJHnUC1QcUrA2LtkyudzRDUWB0S-l4J1oHyReZPdl12D5RwtUjK85mxtaBYQ1zA7a-PvxeJ3Bo1ODMrPM65msPZtpxKO_Taz6i0S8BXBENLo0EJdoQ6dFpGiEcfncgc8yjqToOKCaSSAM_IEidVkepJojc3AwoffKays1HhNPIOp0i8qDsqKkyTWYuMkpT_bg0b5NV7lLB3DUMP_-4lQ5BoUuLE4Xn9mEwblWu9tFaz3IDV1o7NF1NhucEASEnlGEdzXCJicfwDIHrDyNCK682T0jaKzYhltLMe67uCYR5reHoDVwbdmC7Bv4bJ0oztelTxdBYBs7vmgtWvz3Yx9q68mlqy-SA7kXVzRqfeES0xXTTsI_OzdcGq91L8Ruk-9o7G6zMFELbxaSyO7c99bKFxO7GxiCzMmE2mZolAZwqAJlla33TuVfVynYj8A6mcs1qSSFP6vVXbtTyMl2smndHBwFg2mN4kVcodj5VmiKOK1GTkfhxfputWq8nXTU7drh59nB6GNqy4MKWW8m6R2eIjnHHXxzcrt8stvbWoLLkq3MUSHEOHP-fJsbUdz7)

We're less than two weeks from Election Day, and the Democrats have made South Carolina a target. They think Radical Annie can win here.They think this seat is their path to the Senate majority. Let that sink in. South Carolina is the seat that decides whether Chuck Schumer runs the Senate. President Trump is coming to South Carolina because he knows exactly what's at stake. He gave me his "Complete and Total Endorsement," and tonight he's standing on that stage to tell every voter in this state that we are keeping South Carolina red. But Fellow Patriot, a rally doesn't win an election. Turnout does. And turnout takes ads on TV, on phones, and on every screen in South Carolina, running from now until the polls close. Radical Annie and her liberal allies are spending millions to flood our airwaves. If our ads go dark, she fills the silence. Before I take that stage, my team set a goal: We are not there yet, and the doors open in just a few hours. I don't need a handful of max-out checks. we keep our ads on the air, we turn out our voters, and we stop Radical Annie from handing the Senate to the Democrats. So before I walk out to join President Trump tonight, I want to walk out knowing you have my back. Let's keep South Carolina red. Darline Graham P.S. Hey, Peter - it’s Vivek Ramaswamy. **
**By now you probably know that I am running for Governor of Ohio.[ I’m writing to tell you WHY I’m doing it and WHAT is at stake on Election Day.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.__zFKMFQ) **
**President Trump’s decisive re-election in 2024 was more than a political comeback — it was a national gut-check. A repudiation of the corrupt ruling class. A mandate to finally take back control of our country.
As someone who has stood shoulder-to-shoulder with President Trump, I know what it takes to win. And I know what it takes to lead.
[That's why I'm running for Governor of Ohio – to lead the charge in the Buckeye State and make it a model for conservative excellence.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)

This isn't about me - it's about the kind of country we want to leave for our kids. My wife Apoorva and I are raising our three kids in Ohio, and I want to make sure they inherit a state that is strong, proud, and free.**
**[But to do that, we need to shake things up.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.-dqdR22epZxG4Sg) We need to tell the truth, even when it's hard. We need to support President Trump and his America First agenda. We need to overhaul our failing schools, restore our national identity, and reject the victimhood mentality that's holding us back.**
**We need to secure our elections, prosecute voter fraud, and gut the bureaucratic red tape that's strangling our economy. And we need to do it all with courage, conviction, and a commitment to the values that made America great.**
**That's why I'm asking for your support. Whether you live in Ohio or not, I need your help to take on the Democrat machine and the Deep State in in this final stretch before Election Day.
[So, I’m humbly asking you, will you make a contribution of any amount to my campaign right now?](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)

This isn't just about winning an election - it's about sending a message. It's about showing the world that we're not afraid to stand up for what we believe in, even when it's hard. And it's about leaving a legacy that will outlast us all.**
**[So what do you say? Will you join me in this fight? Will you help me make Ohio the leader of America's revival?](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)**
**Let's do this.**
**Sincerely, Vivek Ramaswamy

**Patriot, it’s John James. **
We're less than 3 weeks away from Election Day. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. _I promise I will not waste your time._

clean_body: This will only take 2 minutes.| | | | | Patriot, it’s John James. We're less than 3 weeks away from Election Day. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. I promise I will not waste your time. I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted. I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, I would live it. Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army. During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud. After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician... I saw the Democrats destroying our country, and I knew my service to this great nation wasn’t over yet. Everybody told me running for office isn’t easy, but my heart was telling me it was the right thing to do. I won my election, with the help of President Trump, and started delivering results for my new constituents. Then, in 2023, when the Establishment tried to move on from Trump and being MAGA was seen as risky or politically inconvenient, I was among the first in Michigan to endorse President Trump for 2024. Loyalty isn’t a talking point to me; it’s the only way I know how to operate. My dedication to this country, my loyalty towards my constituents, and my desire to see the greatest nation on earth excel are part of the reasons why I’m now emailing you, but they’re not my #1 reason why... These three kids are the reason why I’m sending this message to you, as a TRUMP-ENDORSED Republican and father running to be the next governor of Michigan Having my own family taught me more lessons than I could list, and it was the one thing being in the U.S. Army didn’t prepare me for. But it also awoke in me a desire to do EVERYTHING and ANYTHING I can to ensure my kids have bright futures. My family means everything to me, and Michigan is our home; that’s why I will fight like my life depends on it to save this state and win this November. I’m under no illusions; I know this election will be one of the toughest challenges I’ve faced in my entire life, but after everything I’ve done in my service, it’s nothing I can’t handle. Unfortunately, the one thing I can’t directly control is spending, and the Democrats will do everything in their power to stop my campaign from making it to the ballot box this November. Nothing can stop us from saving this country if we stand together. Today, I’m asking you to make a small-dollar gift of $10, $25, $50 or ANYTHING you can spare to fuel my campaign’s fight as we approach our upcoming November 3rd election. Thank you for taking the time to read my message. I hope to hear from you in the days to come. ### Dear Peter,

### My annual Fall Luncheon is tomorrow in Daly City from 12:00-1:30pm. Are you able to join us?

Every year, I look forward to gathering with family, friends, supporters, and neighbors for this lunch. It’s a special opportunity to check in with the community that has been there for me since day one.

With the midterm elections right around the corner, and the busy holiday schedule approaching, this event allows us to catch up, discuss next year’s Democratic priorities, and finish strong during the final GOTV sprint.

| | When I first ran for Congress, I promised to fight for our future. My work in Congress has focused on supporting working families, protecting our democracy, and lowering the sky rocketing cost of living.

We’ve made real progress together. We’ve worked to expand access to critical social services for families, invest in local infrastructure projects, and create good-paying jobs to build the next generation of clean energy. But Donald Trump is threatening our progress with draconian funding cuts, foreign military interventions, and corrupt self dealing.

The truth is, our work is far from finished. My campaign has always been powered by local, grassroots supporters. I rely on people like you who believe in the mission and are willing to pitch in a few dollars to keep it going.
By RSVPing to tomorrow’s lunch, you can help Democrats win back the House, stop Donald Trump’s recklessness, and bring stability back to America. I hope to see you there.

For more info contact Carol Ong at [ong102825@aol.com](mailto:ong102825@aol.com).

The size of your gift matters less to me than the number of people who give. When Hollywood sees thousands of Texans and patriots across the country stepping up with , they'll know Texas isn't for sale. In a legal threat issued to Drop Site News last week, attorneys representing former Rep. Mike Rogers and Kristi Rogers took issue [with our recent reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/eeff6e01-5acc-4b4a-941a-3531d047f7a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Aegis, a security firm whose American subsidiary was run by Kristi Rogers, was the recipient of major U.S. contracts--in particular, a $1.017 billion contract to protect the Embassy in Kabul, Afghanistan--including while Rogers was chair of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.
Rogers is the Republican candidate for Senate in Michigan. Drop Site reported that Aegis had done work in Libya and was pursuing further contracts at the same time that Rogers was overseeing an investigation into the 2012 attack on a U.S. compound that killed four Americans, including Ambassador Chris Stevens.
The attorneys argued it was defamatory to report:
> **That Aegis, under Mrs. Rogers 's leadership, performed U.S. government work in Libya and was connected to the September 2012 attack on the U.S. compound in Benghazi. **The Article's section on Libya states that "[t]he pursuit of further contracts took Aegis to Libya," describes Aegis's presence in Tripoli, and then immediately recounts the tragic Benghazi terrorist attack, followed by a section titled "After Benghazi" that discusses Mrs. Rogers and her company. The clear implication is that Aegis, and Mrs. Rogers, held a U.S. government contract in Libya and bore some responsibility for the events in Benghazi. That is false. Neither Mrs. Rogers, Aegis LLC, nor any Aegis entity has ever entered into a contract with any department of the U.S. government to perform work in Libya, and none was involved in the Benghazi attack. [_Bold in the original._]
In fact, Drop Site's article does not assert, either directly or by implication, that Aegis performed "U.S. government work in Libya" under Kristi Rogers's leadership, or that it "was connected to the September 2012 attack on the U.S. compound in Benghazi." Rather, [Drop Site reported the company ](https://substack.com/redirect/eeff6e01-5acc-4b4a-941a-3531d047f7a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)was operating in Libya, [a fact about which the public record is clear,](https://substack.com/redirect/46660e6f-ebc3-46d8-b3ac-f7e4a3871cbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and that it had assessed Benghazi in the summer before the attack on the U.S. compound. Aegis Advisory Services, an intelligence arm of Aegis, had boots on the ground in Libya.

[](https://substack.com/redirect/eeff6e01-5acc-4b4a-941a-3531d047f7a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Mike Rogers's Wife Raked in Lucrative Government Security Contracts While Rogers Served as Intel Chair](https://substack.com/redirect/eeff6e01-5acc-4b4a-941a-3531d047f7a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| [| Read full story

The key reason to include Aegis's Libya work in the article was to show that Aegis was doing work in an area where Rogers was investigating, yet Aegis was never called in for questioning. The source of funding for Aegis's work in Libya, for the purposes of the article, is entirely irrelevant.
Kristi Rogers and her firm's employees were covered by a "no interaction" policy with the committee her husband chaired at the time, according to [a HPSCI spokesperson](https://substack.com/redirect/519b48ab-923b-412e-97e5-8cd3e6b9e789?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the time. The same lawyerly prose was repeated in the legal threat to Drop Site News, which noted that the Rogers' had a "strictly observed and enforced" policy of "no interaction with Mrs. Rogers on any matter relating to the official business of the House" and "no interaction between the Committee and any representative of Aegis."
In the end, there was a firewall for the entire committee and employees of Aegis (as opposed to, for example, Rogers recusing himself) and nobody from Aegis Advisory testified, despite the intelligence firm having on-the-ground intelligence in Libya prior to the attack on the Benghazi outpost. Conservatives looking for a more far-reaching investigation criticized the decision to wall off Aegis from the investigation at the time. See, for instance, Micha Morrison's "Unraveling Benghazi: Is Mike Rogers the Problem?" in Judicial Watch, republished by the Daily Caller.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cd87e160-ce18-4603-bfc9-8eb2e75f770e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The cover page from Aegis Advisory's Libya Briefing, July 2011.
## **Aegis in Libya**
In July 2011, Aegis produced a briefing on Libya that was circulated by Stratfor, an elite private intelligence firm based in Austin, Texas. Stratfor's work, as Morrison noted in Judicial Watch at the time, is used by corporate, military, and government clients, [including the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency](https://substack.com/redirect/258eadbe-840f-44d0-a8fa-aad665477311?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but also the Departments of Defense and Homeland Security.
The Aegis Advisory Libya briefing from July 2011, along with Stratfor's email communications, was [published by Wikileaks](https://substack.com/redirect/96fdb8e5-c46d-4d37-acd4-a8cf14dd115c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The Aegis report was sent to Stratfor's so-called "Alpha List," an elite circle of intelligence professionals.
Under a heading titled, "Libya: Preparing for Life After Qaddafi," the [report by Aegis Advisory](https://substack.com/redirect/96fdb8e5-c46d-4d37-acd4-a8cf14dd115c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) begins: "Richard Ayton, director at Aegis Advisory, travelled to Benghazi in April and May 2011 to examine the situation in the rebel-held east of Libya at first hand. Here is his assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of the National Transitional Council, the role of the revolutionary militias, the international presence in the region and the prospects for a post-Qaddafi government."
In response to a request for comment about why Aegis's intelligence briefing was not included, despite the fact that it circulated via Stratfor to the highest levels of the intelligence community, Abby Rosner, a spokesperson for the Mike Rogers campaign, said:
> Under Mike Rogers' leadership, the House Intelligence Committee interviewed every single member of the intelligence community who was in the fight in Benghazi. Because it is not within its jurisdiction, the Committee did not interview Department of State or Department of Defense personnel. As our counsel mentioned in their October 15, 2026 letter demanding retraction of the false and defamatory statements made in your October 13, 2026 article, "Neither Mrs. Rogers, Aegis LLC, nor any Aegis entity has ever entered into a contract with any department of the U.S. government to perform work in Libya, and none was involved in the Benghazi attack."
This statement from Rogers' campaign to Drop Site is in line with comments by HPSCI in 2014. Committee spokesperson Susan Phalen specifically denied that Rogers a conflict of interest in the Benghazi investigation, claiming that HPSCI did not oversee State Department embassy security.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e794d2d4-7799-420b-88df-7df5ee708566?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Full HPSCI statement on former Rep. Mike Rogers and the Benghazi investigation.
Yet whether in its jurisdiction or not, the final Rogers report quite explicitly targeted the State Department, criticizing then-Secretary of State Hillary Clinton for lapses that led to the deaths:
> "Finding #3: State Department security personnel, resources, and equipment were unable to counter the terrorist threat that day, and they required CIA assistance. Although HPSCI generally does not review State Department security capabilities, and this review did not set out to review those capabilities, evidence the Committee received related to the level of the State Department's security capabilities in Benghazi. CIA security personnel testified that State Department DS agents repeatedly stated they felt ill-equipped and ill-trained to contend with the threat environment in Benghazi. According to eyewitnesses testifying before HPSCI, the DS agents knew well before the attacks that they could not defend the TMF against an armed assault. The DS agents also told CIA about their requests for additional resources."
Chairman Rogers also mentioned the inadequacy of the ragtag local militias subcontracted by the State Department to defend the compound, including the February 17th Brigade. Aegis, in its 2011 Libya briefing, addressed the February 17th Brigade and its role in the Libyan uprising. "The State Department had contracted with the February 17th Brigade and the Blue Mountain Group to provide local security for the [compound]," the report states. "All available information indicates that the February 17th Brigade guards were inside the walls of the compound and did not detect or report information about the attackers before the attackers breached the gate."
Why did the February 17th Brigade not detect or report such information? What else was known about them? Had the committee wanted to learn more about the February 17th Brigade in Benghazi, one avenue would have been to call Aegis officials.
Enmity against Gaddafi was unifying the opposition, Aegis reported, but that would fray once he was gone. "At present the February 17th militias are united by a common cause: the removal of Qaddafi and the unification of the country," Aegis assessed. "However, once Qaddafi has gone--and the rebels have spilt too much blood to countenance a deal that would involve his maintaining any political role--this unity will be threatened."
The committee did not call Richard Ayton, who was on the ground in Libya pre-attack; Sarah Keeling, Managing Director of Aegis Advisory Services; or Pandora Crawly, Business Development Manager for Aegis Advisory, whose contacts were listed on the Libya Briefing; nor were any employees of Aegis called in for Mike Rogers's investigation.

**Thank you for being by my side in this fight, for sticking up for working people, for powering the change we urgently need here in Ohio and across the country.**
I know my team and I ask a lot of you, and these emails can get pesky. But please know that whether you pitch in $1 or $100, or even just take the time to read our messages, you’re making a big impact on our campaign.
We’ve got 13 days to go and millions of voters left to reach. I’m grateful to have your support throughout it all. Thanks so much.
More soon.

The Guardian is reporting that Elon Musk has personally spent a whopping $366 million to elect right-wing candidates. The richest person in the world is now putting his power, wealth, and influence directly to use to support one party. And what makes this more concerning is that he’s targeting battleground races that could determine whether fair maps, equal representation, and voting rights are protected in the future.
They know we can’t outraise their millions. But here’s what I know: the power of the people can beat billionaire power.

Then I went public.| | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141906173/655132344/-323302678?refcode=261012_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMmNhMDM2OTUtOGRjZC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=DaGYP7mqfR3-y2j8gW5Rg_DgRSlxlO1WZRJs_AaNHco=)

**I never imagined that I would become one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken opponents.**

I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home.

I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country.

After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents.

Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser.

I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first.

Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors.

**I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country.**

Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump?

For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening.

But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question:

Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous?

In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public.

I was terrified.

I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence.

But silence costs more.

So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat.

Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue.

I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first.

Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences.

**That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild.**

Resist Reclaim Rebuild is a group of Democratic activists working to defeat MAGA candidates in the battleground races that will determine whether Donald Trump continues to enjoy virtually unchecked power -- or whether we elect a Congress capable of standing up to him.

They understand that resistance cannot exist only in speeches, television interviews, or social media posts.

It MUST reach the ballot box.

It MUST be organized.

And it MUST be focused on the races where a relatively small number of votes could mean the difference between a MAGA rubber stamp and a real check on Donald Trump’s power.

[**So, I'm asking personally: Will you donate $10, $25 or whatever you can afford today to help Resist Reclaim Rebuild defeat MAGA in the battleground races that matter most?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141906174/655132345/-323302678?refcode=261012_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMmNhMDM2OTUtOGRjZC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=DaGYP7mqfR3-y2j8gW5Rg_DgRSlxlO1WZRJs_AaNHco=)[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141906175/655132346/949025562?refcode=261012_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMmNhMDM2OTUtOGRjZC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=DaGYP7mqfR3-y2j8gW5Rg_DgRSlxlO1WZRJs_AaNHco=)

MAGA wants us exhausted. They want every new outrage to make us feel a little more powerless. They want us to believe that one person speaking out, casting a ballot or making a contribution cannot possibly change anything.

I learned the opposite.

I learned that courage is contagious.

Control of Congress could come down to only a handful of seats. Your contribution can help elect Democrats who will defend our Constitution, demand accountability and finally place a meaningful check on Trump’s unfettered power.

Please help Resist Reclaim Rebuild fight for those victories today.

Peter, Last week Trump handed a dictator everything he wanted. Days before the toughest bipartisan Russia sanctions in a generation were meant to hit Russia, _he waived them all_. Putin's reward for invading his neighbors, bombing cities, and stealing Ukrainian children is a diesel deal and a president who runs interference for him. Trump's administration even restricted the satellite support Ukraine uses to shoot down Russian drones. **Now Trump wants the world to applaud him for brokering "peace" in the same war he just bankrolled, pushing a deal that only helps the dictator keep what he stole.**
---
[ **No rewards for despots. Flip TX-03.** ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8-ClP7QRjDKc3eEpOK4gbSZ8Vty7QJp14V5-p2jQLhsIxJ7WevFaKQb9L1SBwIDjviiDra3_T9NhOyrpvyNmMLfmFclIEFiZ5sN8xqVAfAUtbzHGyRKmyvmQeYGfBRsNyz3jK-1crOgEj9kXTaIRU62AvJ8HKkY9SzkjOpGpf8tYBEBMDcVhb6PF151MIil2jeX6fzUeh4EYvasqL50MyMeu-yUtadExOnQqqlh_zoBvfL-utU8WZkNi4lQCrBBWAR6En-ReqjbMM11xgUTGhyh-JXxhv9H-dtY5vt4ZMn9ijth1pxXfSA4v50f5ZZZnRnysUAKKsdfI61qhRuG22g8/4v2/aBBW8jnuREmlrly9lrcbjw/h1/h001.u69Bj7lN8H32_wPHPkwZA8aeQB_WJj4F-852d43ikWM)

I spent 20 years in uniform fighting despotism.
I flew combat missions because America decided generations ago that violent authoritarians who devour free countries must be stopped.
I watched friends sacrifice everything for that principle.
Nobody who wore the uniform signed up to watch an American president kneel to the Kremlin.
And Keith Self, a veteran himself, shamefully bows right along with Trump.

Friends,
For four years, Mike Lawler has had the chance to make life easier for Hudson Valley families. Instead, he has only made it harder and more expensive by voting with Donald Trump 100% of the time, even when it harms all of us. Mike promised he wouldn’t cut Medicaid, then cast the deciding vote for the largest Medicaid cut in American history. That vote has thrown nearly half a million New Yorkers off their healthcare — including 37,000 in our district alone — while monthly premiums have climbed by as much as 50%. Mike voted eight times for Trump’s reckless tariffs, which are costing Hudson Valley families an extra $4,200. He also voted six times to continue Trump’s war of choice with Iran, even as 21 American service members have lost their lives and gas prices have hit $4.50 a gallon. Then there’s SALT. The tax deduction cap that Trump created to punish New Yorkers in 2017 was set to expire at the end of 2025. Instead, Mike voted to make it a permanent tax on working families to fund tax breaks for billionaires. Worst of all? He dares to call that a win. **Mike Lawler’s disastrous record demonstrates one thing: he’s looking out for his corporate and special interest backers, NOT us.** I spent 16 years in the Army fighting for every American, regardless of how they registered to vote, and I served under both Republican and Democratic presidents. No one will stand in my way of creating a better, more affordable future for the Hudson Valley. **Two weeks to go. Let’s bring it home.** With gratitude and fire,
Cait Conley

clean_body: | | | | Friends, For four years, Mike Lawler has had the chance to make life easier for Hudson Valley families. Instead, he has only made it harder and more expensive by voting with Donald Trump 100% of the time, even when it harms all of us. Mike promised he wouldn’t cut Medicaid, then cast the deciding vote for the largest Medicaid cut in American history. That vote has thrown nearly half a million New Yorkers off their healthcare — including 37,000 in our district alone — while monthly premiums have climbed by as much as 50%. Mike voted eight times for Trump’s reckless tariffs, which are costing Hudson Valley families an extra $4,200. He also voted six times to continue Trump’s war of choice with Iran, even as 21 American service members have lost their lives and gas prices have hit $4.50 a gallon. Then there’s SALT. The tax deduction cap that Trump created to punish New Yorkers in 2017 was set to expire at the end of 2025. Instead, Mike voted to make it a permanent tax on working families to fund tax breaks for billionaires. Worst of all? He dares to call that a win. Mike Lawler’s disastrous record demonstrates one thing: he’s looking out for his corporate and special interest backers, NOT us. I spent 16 years in the Army fighting for every American, regardless of how they registered to vote, and I served under both Republican and Democratic presidents. subject: Trump’s Justice Department just sued California

| Trump’s classic playbook: sow doubt, target a blue state, hope the lie outruns the correction before Election Day.

[](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/8022?amount=10&t=1&refcode=aschiff_email_102126_antidoterefresh&akid=10851%2E5257348%2Ey3zXvt)
Derek, Trump's Justice Department just sued California, asking a judge to block more than 20,000 mail ballots from voters the administration alleges are likely noncitizens. The administration handed over the names on a thumb drive. Los Angeles County officials refused to open it, citing basic data privacy and security protocols. Now, the AP is reporting that the Justice Department has arrested more than two dozen noncitizens to buttress their claims of widespread voter fraud right before the election. But these isolated cases — out of more than 20 million ballots in California — do not support their argument. There has never been evidence of the systemic fraud they allege, let alone fraud affecting the outcome of any election. This isn't the first time Trump has tried to silence California voters — not even this year. Over the summer, the Trump administration claimed 190,000 noncitizens were on California's rolls. After state officials disputed it, a Reuters investigation found just 129 people prosecuted for noncitizen voting nationwide since 1996. Derek, none of this is about stopping noncitizen voting. It's Trump's classic playbook: **sow doubt, target a blue state, watch the lie catch fire, and then claim the results were fraudulent.** That doubt is a poison, meant to convince you your vote doesn't matter. It does. It has never mattered more. There's only one antidote strong enough to counter it: turnout so large that no purged list or rigged voting system can suppress it. Democrats have never been in a better position to flip the Senate — but we're being vastly outspent by shadowy GOP super PACs in the final weeks of this campaign. Peter,
Our Red-to-Blue races across the country are absolutely critical to win next month. Take a look at this map:
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261021_1_r2b.0_p9Ui&refcode=em20261021-4173&amount=5&t=2&akid=4173%2E587540%2EVJBX-1)
Over the past few months, Leaders We Deserve has been highlighting 18 critical state legislature, House, and Senate races with powerful candidates running to flip red seats blue.
For so long, Republicans have been strategically winning state legislatures, creating supermajorities at the state level. The decisions of so many critical state laws lie in the hands of state legislatures — we can’t neglect the urgency to build progressive power at the state level.
We also have the opportunity to take back both the House and Senate this year. Leaders We Deserve has endorsed Randy Villegas, Kristina Knickerbocker, and Angie Nixon in critical Red-to-Blue races. The momentum has been building, the ratings are shifting in our favor, and now we have to do everything in our power to reach voters and show up strong on Election Day.
This year, we have incredible candidates with the power to flip seats blue, take back the House and Senate, and break Republican majorities in state legislatures. But we need to be able to fully support these candidates _through_ Election Day.
That’s why Leaders We Deserve created our Red-to-Blue Fund. This fund is dedicated to helping elect our endorsed candidates and flipping critical seats. None of our candidates take _any_ corporate PAC money — so we’re counting on your support.
But we’re running out of time. We’ve got less than two weeks to get our campaigns the resources they need to win these races.

Friends,
In just a few hours, I'll be taking the stage against Roger Marshall. Just like I did in our last debate, I'm going to hold him accountable for turning his back on hardworking Kansas families across our state.
Before that, I wanted to take a moment to reach out with a personal note of thanks.
**We 're coming in to this debate with the wind at our backs:**
🏁 Multiple election forecasters, from The Cook Political Report to Nate Silver, Sabato's Crystal Ball and even Steve Kornacki, have **shifted this race to "toss-up."**
🏁 Polls show me with a narrow **lead over Marshall.**
🏁 People on both sides of the aisle have **endorsed my campaign** , including six former Kansas governors -- two of whom are Republicans -- our current governor, lifelong Republican Arch "Pond" Naramore and thousands of people just like you.

But, we haven't gotten here alone. Everything we've accomplished has happened because of our amazing grassroots team. In other words, because of _**you**_.
You've helped drive this campaign forward every time you've read a Substack post. Filled out a survey. Chipped in to our campaign. Talked to a neighbor about why you support me. Helped someone make a plan to vote. Knocked on a door, made a phone call or forwarded one of my emails.
**Your support has made all the difference in getting us to a place where we have a historic opportunity to win this race. And because of you and thousands of people like you, when we win, Kansans will finally have a leader who will put their well-being first and be a true champion for them -- even when doing so is hard.**
You see, that's what a leader does. They stand up for their communities, prioritize people over party and say no to the cruel and chaotic policies that make their constituents' lives harder.
Friends, _real_ leaders don't rubber-stamp slashes to the healthcare assistance that thousands of people rely on. They don't keep us in a war that's driving up gas prices and sending diesel through the roof. And they don't approve disastrous tariffs that cost their people $100+ every month.
You know that, and I know that. But Sen. Marshall has done all these things and more over the past year, which is why I'm going to hold him accountable up there tonight. I'll be speaking up for every single person who feels betrayed by the leader they elected to represent them. But I can't do it alone. Before I take the stage, I need your support one more time.
You see, with early voting underway and Election Day just around the corner, top GOP super PACs are swooping in to try to buy this seat for Roger Marshall. They're spending millions on massive ad buys to turn voters against me just as they're going to the polls.
My team and I have set a $150,000 pre-debate goal to help us fight back against their attacks, fund our get-out-the-vote efforts and make sure every Kansan knows what's at stake here. I wouldn't ask if it wasn't important, but this is a make-or-break moment.
**[Please, if you believe in what we're trying to do, will you pitch in right now to help us reach our goal, keep our ads on the air and flip this seat?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e2a7aa8c-acf9-47be-9a10-ab527bec27d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e2a7aa8c-acf9-47be-9a10-ab527bec27d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for standing with me. Together, we can bring this home.
Adam Hamilton

| | | Peter, I know how often political campaigns are in your inbox asking you for money... So I figured the least I can do is tell you a bit more about **who I am**.
---
**To my son, Aidan:** I’m his mom, his greatest protector, and his biggest supporter.
**To my country:** I’m a proud combat veteran, who served and protected our country, to make the American dream possible for everyone.
**To the district I’m running to represent, AZ-06:** I’m their fighter, ready to take on the special interests and DC Republicans, who are hellbent on stacking the deck against working families like mine.
**And... to Speaker Mike Johnson and DC Republicans:** I’m their worst nightmare. They know I have the grit to flip this seat, and an unstoppable grassroots team behind me to get the job done.
_I’m running for Congress because of Aidan, my love for Arizona, and for our community. And I know that if we stand together, we can win this race, and bring real change to Washington._

| | | | | | Ballots are in mailboxes across Southwest Washington, and votes are already being cast. Thirteen days from now, we decide who represents us and what kind of future we're building here.
I'm running because Southwest Washington needs a representative who has done the work. I served my country in the United States Navy. I built a business in Chehalis that employs our neighbors. And in the State Senate, I've fought for balanced budgets, lower taxes, and working families who are paying more for groceries, gas, and housing while Washington, D.C. keeps making it harder.
Marie Perez has had her chance. Her entire record in Congress is exactly one bill signed into law: the naming of a post office.
You saw the difference again right here at home this month. In Camas, about a dozen high school cross-country girls walked off the course rather than race against a male teammate who started this season on the boys' team. Those girls shouldn't have to choose between competing and competing fairly.
Today, I'm standing with them in Camas, and with the women and girls across Southwest Washington who fought for decades for a level playing field. In Congress, I'll vote to protect women's sports and define participation by biological sex because fairness and safety aren't negotiable.
That's what's at stake: a representative who will fight for affordability, safe communities, and fairness for our daughters, or one who leaves Southwest Washington with a post office naming and no record to stand on.
[Thirteen days. That's all that's left. Can I count on you for $25 or more today?](https://us.list-manage.com/xgDRd4tqp7z?e=90b300faf9&c2id=62222c63d51e1bc08f3d4aa9538aea5e)
Grateful for your support,
John Braun

Before I announced this campaign, I sat down with my sons.
They're not old enough to grasp what a campaign or politics really is. But they know when something serious is happening.
So I told them the truth. We'll be on the road. _A lot._
They might see strangers shouting at dad... I might be out of town some days... They might read nasty headlines about our family -- things that aren't true.

clean_body: They're still too little to understand politics. But I wasn't going to lie to them. | Friend, Before I announced this campaign, I sat down with my sons. They're not old enough to grasp what a campaign or politics really is. But they know when something serious is happening. So I told them the truth. We'll be on the road. A lot. They might see strangers shouting at dad... I might be out of town some days... They might read nasty headlines about our family -- things that aren't true. I promised to always keep them safe, but I also told them the truth: This won 't be easy. But when your country is at a crossroads, you don't hide. You lead. Not because it 's easy. Not because it's safe. But because I refuse to let my sons grow up in a country that no longer believes in itself. Ohio should be the state that leads this nation again -- in education, in industry, in values that matter. I'm fighting for that future. For my family. For yours. For every child who deserves a country worth inheriting. | This isn't just a campaign. It's a mission. Let's win it - together. People walk past a banner depicting the portraits of Iran's former supreme leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini (L), Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei (C), and slain supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei (R) in Tehran on October 21, 2026. Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP via Getty Images.
The U.S. and Israel are preparing to resume attacks on Iran, according to senior Iranian officials and a U.S. official, and may even launch operations before next week's Israeli elections. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is fighting for his political life, and the Israeli press is rife with reports that he is looking for a way to exploit the Iran standoff to his advantage. In the U.S., President Donald Trump's approval ratings are at historic lows, and the midterm elections are less than two weeks away.
Iran's top security official, Gen. Mohsen Rezaei, the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council and personal representative of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, told Drop Site that, in the event of an attack, Iran still has capacity to continue launching missiles and drones at various U.S. assets across the region in retaliation and that it would expand its range of targets.
"If the question is whether Iran still has the ability to continue missile and drone operations, the answer is yes," Rezaei said in an exclusive written interview. "The United States has valuable assets in the region. In the event of war, cables, data centers and artificial intelligence facilities could also come within range. If the conflict begins again, we will have a broader plan."
"Everyone must understand that action against Iran carries a cost," he added. "If diplomacy can bring about that understanding, we prefer diplomacy. But if the war continues, Iran has the tools it needs to keep responding."
A senior Iranian official told Drop Site that Tehran's current internal intelligence assessment indicates a high likelihood that large-scale bombing may even begin before Tuesday's Israeli elections. "Trump has sat on Iran's proposed package for ending the war, and negotiations have stalled," said the official, who is not authorized to speak publicly. "Contrary to the show he is putting on, Trump has no clear or actionable plan for [ending] the war with Iran. This has been the cause of a diplomatic deadlock." He warned that Iran should not be underestimated, claiming, "Should another war against Iran begin, given our knowledge of the patterns of American force deployment in the countries of the region, their casualty figures will be ten times higher."
The White House denied it was planning to strike Iran in the next two weeks. "The United States will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections," White House Principal Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly said in a statement to Drop Site.
Tehran believes Israel would be tasked with firing the first shots, the senior Iranian official said, aimed at "destroying Iran's newly deployed air defense systems, in order to open the path for American bombers." The U.S., he said, would likely focus on attacking Iran's southern defense systems along the Strait of Hormuz and potentially attempt to seize one of the islands off the Iranian mainland after heavy bombing. Trump, he said, is continuing his quest for a notable action that he can use to proclaim victory, adding that Iran believes he may seek to launch a "token" attack on one of Iran's underground nuclear sites, such as Pickaxe Mountain, and subsequently portray it as a definitive blow. "Trump is flat-out lying about Iran's nuclear program," the official said.
A U.S. official confirmed to Drop Site that military assets are being moved rapidly into place in preparation for an expected green light from Trump. Among the American officials pushing for renewed attacks is U.S. Central Command chief Gen. Bradley Cooper, the official said. "CENTCOM is putting all the pieces into place to renew major combat operations," added the official, who is not authorized to discuss war plans. He was skeptical the war would resume before the Israeli elections, but conceded, "We did start Epic Fury without all our assets in place."
The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier and the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit are [heading](https://substack.com/redirect/a4adbf2a-1fbf-4d62-a98c-4ee057133812?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the Middle East, bringing approximately 10,000 additional sailors and Marines to the region. The Roosevelt, which departed Japan on Monday, could reach the region by the end of next week ahead of its initially expected deployment slated for late November. It will join the USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington, both currently in the Arabian Sea.
While the U.S. official said the likelihood of new U.S.-Israeli attacks was high, he acknowledged that Trump has gone to the brink of military action and pulled back more times than is publicly known. "Trump has backed off major combat operations against Iran or the Houthis seven times since July," the U.S. official said, referring to Ansarallah, who launched a major offensive against Saudi-backed groups in Yemen. "At the last minute, he calls it off."
Netanyahu, who is behind in the polls, claimed Wednesday without evidence that Iran was actively working on the development of a nuclear weapon and said he had ordered the Israeli military to prepare for preemptive action. "The Iranian regime still has not learned its lesson. Mojtaba Khamenei decided to follow in his father's footsteps. He has taken off the safety, and Iran is once again trying to develop its weapons of death," Netanyahu said. "There is only one way to remove this threat once and for all, to topple the regime in Iran, and that is my directive to the IDF, the Mossad and the security agencies."

Analysts say that Trump is continuing to pursue an elusive clean victory narrative, while Netanyahu understands this may be his last chance at continuing the war he has agitated for his entire political career.
"This is Netanyahu's last chance to do so. And he's not going to leave until he turns every stone to be able to achieve it. Particularly knowing that either his career is going to end or the United States is going to go in a direction in which this no longer will be an option," said Trita Parsi, a leading Iran expert and the executive Vice President of the Quincy Institute. "Trump, I suspect, has already made a decision that he's going to go to war," he added. "The Israelis have been very successful playing to his psychology, which is that he's willing to take massive risks as long as he has the belief that it can get him a victory so that he avoids accepting defeat, which is so crucial for him. But it is a massive miscalculation that will make the situation 100 times worse."
The intersection of Trump's and Netanyahu's political interests increases the chances that the war will resume, argues former senior U.S. Iran negotiator Robert Malley. "Netanyahu may want a longer campaign with broader objectives. Trump may want something shorter that he could quickly get out of. The overlap between the two might well be an intensive campaign that doesn't last too long," said Malley, a key figure in brokering the 2015 Iran nuclear deal. "President Trump may want a victory lap and an exit ramp. But as has been proven time and time again, the exit is not decided by him alone," said Malley, who currently directs the Middle East Program at the International Crisis Group. "There is every reason to believe the Iranians are preparing all kinds of steps, whether by them or by their regional partners, whether in or out of theater, to ensure that however much he wants a victory lap and an exit ramp, he is deprived of both."
## **" We Are Prepared for the Next Stage"**
Gen. Rezaei is one of the most prominent military figures in modern Iranian history. A former commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, he was tapped to serve as the top military advisor to Khamenei in August. His comments are often viewed as reflecting the consensus at the top of Iran's power structure. He told Drop Site that despite U.S. claims to have "obliterated" or "decimated" Iran's military infrastructure, Iran spent decades preparing for a broader war waged by the U.S.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b8aefcc8-d0e6-49ee-aea4-01b611baaab5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Gen. Mohsen Rezaei attends a ceremony at Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini's shrine in southern Tehran, Iran, on June 4, 2026. Photo by Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images.
"Iran has invested for years in building redundancy into these capabilities: dispersed production, underground facilities, different launch systems and the ability to repair damage and replace losses," Rezaei told Drop Site. "More importantly, you should not assess our capacity solely by asking how many missiles remain in storage. In a prolonged war, the central question is whether a country can sustain a continuous cycle of production, deployment and response. We have shown that, even months after the war began, we can still impose costs on the other side."
Rezaei also indicated that Tehran would deploy new capabilities in its retaliatory response. "We did not deploy all our capabilities in the previous stages. We brought more capabilities into operation in proportion to the intensity of the war, and we are also prepared for the next stage," Rezaei said.
During the war, Iran carried out at least 135 drone and missile strikes on 84 critical infrastructure sites across seven countries--Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Iraq, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, and Bahrain, according to a [Reuters investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/05cb591e-e8e0-4b06-98b9-4528b2b2bb2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). While Gulf governments repeatedly attributed the damage to falling debris from intercepted Iranian missiles and drones, the investigation found evidence of deliberate, precision strikes targeting critical equipment. The attacks demonstrated "precision, targeting expertise, and patience," Ryan Stevens, a former U.S. Marine Corps special operations airstrike coordinator, told Reuters.
Echoing Rezaei's warning about communications infrastructure, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesperson, Hossein Mohebi, also threatened to target internet cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. launched renewed attacks. Mohebi further [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/46901c8c-eec7-4f5a-988e-74399c4d3418?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday that another U.S. military operation would trigger a global energy crisis. "If America takes a new action--even a limited one--the world will face a serious energy crisis," he told the Tehran Times.
Rezaei did not rule out targeting energy infrastructure in Gulf states as a retaliatory measure. "If the U.S. strategy is to prolong the war while using neighboring countries' energy infrastructure to offset the pressure arising from Hormuz and maintain the blockade of Iran, those governments should not assume they can participate in economic warfare against Iran without putting themselves at risk," he said. "The message is not that Iran wants to destroy the Persian Gulf's energy system. The message is that there can be no arrangement in which Iran's economic lifelines come under attack while the economic architecture enabling those attacks is considered untouched and immune."
The senior Iranian official said Trump's approach to Iran has been focused on short-term objectives that are often disconnected from geopolitical realities or core U.S. interests, likening him to a day trader. "The wartime secrecy surrounding military operations has given him and his family exclusive and extraordinary access to information regarding forthcoming actions and the state of the markets--access that benefits only those closest to him," he said. "Perpetuating the current situation will carry strategic consequences, not least that the energy markets will not find calm for the next three years. The continuation of this war has shifted the dynamics of relations in Iran's favor, as the littoral states of the Persian Gulf are rapidly redefining their relationship with Iran, having become convinced that the U.S. military is incapable of defending its own bases, this at a time when those same states had expected America to defend their countries."
Iranian officials have said repeatedly that Iran will not back away from its red lines in any negotiations, consistently pointing to Tehran's acceptance of the June 17 Memorandum of Understanding, which was swiftly violated by the U.S., leading to a breakdown in the diplomatic process in early July.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he presented a "Seven-Day Plan" to the U.S. through mediators at last month's UN General Assembly, outlining steps for an end to the war and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. "Under this proposal, the U.S. would not be expected to do anything that it has not already agreed to," Araghchi [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/4631c90a-19d9-4d16-b6c0-deca57e4d6c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in an op-ed for the Financial Times on Wednesday. He said the framework's steps and outcome were clear: "The Strait would reopen on Day 6, with the resumption of talks for a final deal commencing on Day 7." Araghchi [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/5523844e-256f-474b-b216-54bab839c307?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in an interview with Iraqi television that the U.S. had accepted the seven-day proposal but requested the addition of a "few more clauses," adding that diplomatic contacts through mediators remain ongoing.
"As President Trump stated, Iran is in very bad condition, both economically and militarily, and the blockade will remain in full force and effect, with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait," Kelly told Drop Site in a statement.
Rezaei told Drop Site that Iran's negotiating strategy has evolved as a result of Trump's unreliability. "We will not return to our previous approach to diplomacy, but we will not abandon diplomacy either. We have presented seven new conditions through intermediaries. Until those conditions are fulfilled, Iran will neither reopen the strait nor return to negotiations," Rezaei said. "The first memorandum failed because the commitments were implemented in the wrong order. We opened the strait and maritime traffic resumed, but the other side's political and economic commitments were not implemented in a way that could sustain the agreement. Once the United States obtained what it immediately needed, the balance of leverage shifted. That experience matters to us."
"If Washington honors its commitments, there is a path to reopening the Strait of Hormuz and continuing diplomacy," he continued. "But Iran will not first give up the leverage that brought the other side to the negotiating table and then wait to see whether its promises are fulfilled."
Parsi said that Iran is not eager to resume the war, but has recognized that the diplomatic track has been treated by the U.S. as an ultimatum operation masquerading as negotiations. "Their conclusion--based on extensive experience with Trump now--is that he simply won't back off unless his policy is reaching a cost to him that is intolerable. And that it's not concessions or face saving exits that will get Trump to back off, but simply that the policy becomes too costly."
Attacks on ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz have surged to a record high in recent weeks, with more than two dozen vessels reporting attacks so far in October, according to data released Friday by the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency. The agency said the actual number was likely far higher, as the "majority of vessels attacked" were refusing to report incidents.
The IRGC reported further attacks over the weekend and into Tuesday, including a supertanker carrying two million barrels of oil struck Saturday, another tanker hit Sunday, and two tankers that it said caught fire Tuesday after striking naval mines south of the Strait. Iran says it is targeting vessels violating its maritime restrictions or using unauthorized shipping routes.
"Over the past two or three months, we have struck an average of five vessels belonging to these smugglers every night," Rezaei said. "Smuggling is taking place along the southern edge of the strait at enormous cost and with considerable risk. Trump then says the Strait of Hormuz is open."
Despite the escalating attacks, oil exports from the Middle East appear to have rebounded past prewar levels, primarily through tanker-to-tanker transfers in the Gulf of Oman, and expanded use of Saudi and Emirati pipelines bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. However, oil prices remain high, hovering well above $100 per barrel of Brent crude amid fears of the ongoing attacks and diminishing U.S. fuel stockpiles. "The current price of oil reflects the reality," Rezaei said.
"The management of Hormuz is a national asset for us, and this is not simply about collecting tolls. The main issue is security," he continued. "Charges can also be collected for security, insurance and environmental costs, but the importance of managing the strait goes far beyond the revenue it generates," he said. "We will continue managing it to maintain peace and security in the region, and we will not back down from this position."
The senior Iranian official said that the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz "has become the new pretext--the nuclear issue, previously, was a lie upon which the war was launched--for the United States to prolong the war." Trump, he charged, "has fallen into the trap of prolonging what was advertised as the shortest of wars." A "war of attrition," he said, "will work to Iran's advantage and to America's detriment."
The war has had a devastating impact on Iran's economy. As part of its escalation over the summer, the U.S. reimposed a blockade on Iran's southern ports and launched a new campaign of sanctions dubbed Operation Economic Outcast. The Iranian rial subsequently collapsed, falling to record lows, making imports dramatically more expensive and imposing even more scarcity on people in Iran.
"Iran will suffer from a prolonged blockade; anyone who says otherwise is not being realistic. Families will bear the costs, investment will suffer, and sustaining some sectors of the economy will become more difficult. But economic pain and strategic collapse are not the same thing," Rezaei said. "Washington has repeatedly made the mistake of assuming that, if it can make life inside Iran difficult enough, Iran's political system will consequently accept America's strategic demands. These are two different calculations."
"Our goal is not to make it to 2029. Our goal is to end the war on terms that reduce the likelihood of another war."

The U.S. and Israel are preparing to resume attacks on Iran, according to senior Iranian officials and a U.S. official, and may even launch operations before next week's Israeli elections. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is fighting for his political life, and the Israeli press is rife with reports that he is looking for a way to exploit the Iran standoff to his advantage. In the U.S., President Donald Trump's approval ratings are at historic lows, and the midterm elections are less than two weeks away. Iran's top security official, Gen. Mohsen Rezaei, the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council and personal representative of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, told Drop Site that, in the event of an attack, Iran still has capacity to continue launching missiles and drones at various U.S. assets across the region in retaliation and that it would expand its range of targets. "If the question is whether Iran still has the ability to continue missile and drone operations, the answer is yes," Rezaei said in an exclusive written interview. "The United States has valuable assets in the region. In the event of war, cables, data centers and artificial intelligence facilities could also come within range. If the conflict begins again, we will have a broader plan." "Everyone must understand that action against Iran carries a cost," he added. "If diplomacy can bring about that understanding, we prefer diplomacy. But if the war continues, Iran has the tools it needs to keep responding." A senior Iranian official told Drop Site that Tehran's current internal intelligence assessment indicates a high likelihood that large-scale bombing may even begin before Tuesday's Israeli elections. "Trump has sat on Iran's proposed package for ending the war, and negotiations have stalled," said the official, who is not authorized to speak publicly. "Contrary to the show he is putting on, Trump has no clear or actionable plan for [ending] the war with Iran. This has been the cause of a diplomatic deadlock." He warned that Iran should not be underestimated, claiming, "Should another war against Iran begin, given our knowledge of the patterns of American force deployment in the countries of the region, their casualty figures will be ten times higher." The White House denied it was planning to strike Iran in the next two weeks. "The United States will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections," White House Principal Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly said in a statement to Drop Site. Tehran believes Israel would be tasked with firing the first shots, the senior Iranian official said, aimed at "destroying Iran's newly deployed air defense systems, in order to open the path for American bombers." The U.S., he said, would likely focus on attacking Iran's southern defense systems along the Strait of Hormuz and potentially attempt to seize one of the islands off the Iranian mainland after heavy bombing. Trump, he said, is continuing his quest for a notable action that he can use to proclaim victory, adding that Iran believes he may seek to launch a "token" attack on one of Iran's underground nuclear sites, such as Pickaxe Mountain, and subsequently portray it as a definitive blow. "Trump is flat-out lying about Iran's nuclear program," the official said. A U.S. official confirmed to Drop Site that military assets are being moved rapidly into place in preparation for an expected green light from Trump. Among the American officials pushing for renewed attacks is U.S. Central Command chief Gen. Bradley Cooper, the official said. "CENTCOM is putting all the pieces into place to renew major combat operations," added the official, who is not authorized to discuss war plans. He was skeptical the war would resume before the Israeli elections, but conceded, "We did start Epic Fury without all our assets in place." The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier and the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit are to the Middle East, bringing approximately 10,000 additional sailors and Marines to the region. The Roosevelt, which departed Japan on Monday, could reach the region by the end of next week ahead of its initially expected deployment slated for late November. It will join the USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington, both currently in the Arabian Sea. While the U.S. official said the likelihood of new U.S.-Israeli attacks was high, he acknowledged that Trump has gone to the brink of military action and pulled back more times than is publicly known. "Trump has backed off major combat operations against Iran or the Houthis seven times since July," the U.S. official said, referring to Ansarallah, who launched a major offensive against Saudi-backed groups in Yemen. "At the last minute, he calls it off." Netanyahu, who is behind in the polls, claimed Wednesday without evidence that Iran was actively working on the development of a nuclear weapon and said he had ordered the Israeli military to prepare for preemptive action. "The Iranian regime still has not learned its lesson. Mojtaba Khamenei decided to follow in his father's footsteps. He has taken off the safety, and Iran is once again trying to develop its weapons of death," Netanyahu said. "There is only one way to remove this threat once and for all, to topple the regime in Iran, and that is my directive to the IDF, the Mossad and the security agencies."
